prerequisites: Solid knowledge of concepts from the Signals Theory course: Fourier theory of periodic and aperiodic deterministic signals, random variables, stochastic processes and their spectral analysis.
Basic knowledge of courses in the telecommunications sector provided in the degree program.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the basic principles of telecommunications, the characteristics of the signals used and their propagation modes.
Knowledge and understanding of the different systems of analog and digital modulation and demodulation of signals.
Knowledge and understanding of the disturbances affecting received signals and their statistical characterization.
Knowledge and understanding of the main aspects of TCP/IP networks and networks with ISO/OSI architecture.
Ability to classify existing or soon-to-be-developed telecommunication networks in relation to specific operational requirements.
Ability to understand the functioning of the basic devices of a network.
Ability to define appropriate types of sensor networks.
Ability to select MAC and Network level algorithms in relation to specific application needs.
Ability to characterize, analyze and quantify disturbances on signals and their effects.
Ability to comparatively and critically analyze the different transmission and reception, modulation and demodulation schemes.
Ability to analyze and model the main protocol architectures.
Ability to make autonomous choices regarding the design of an analog or digital telecommunications system.
Ability to clearly and rigorously present telecommunication network architectures and their applications.
Ability to logically present demonstrations related to the characterization of signals and random disturbances.
Ability to logically present technical demonstrations on characteristics of specific telecommunication systems and networks.
Ability to autonomously carry out the complete characterization of a telecommunications system.
Ability to autonomously find technical documentation on network protocols and services.

syllabus_topics: Transmission through modulation of analog and digital signals
Efficiency of modulation/demodulation schemes against noise
Principles and applications of sensor and actuator networks
Routing techniques in wired and wireless networks

Introduction to communication systems: information and disturbance, information sources, communication system architecture, wireless and wired communication systems, frequency allocation, notes on signal propagation mode, with particular reference to wireless systems
Disturbances in communication systems: band-limited white noise, thermal noise, noise figure, equivalent noise temperature, noise figure of cascaded systems

Analog modulations: classic AM modulation, AM-DSB modulation, AM-SSB modulation, angular modulations (PM and FM). Modulators and demodulators, performance against noise, threshold effect. Signal multiplexing: FDM and TDM. Superheterodyne and homodyne receivers

Digital modulations: baseband impulse modulations: "flat top" and "natural gating" PAM, PDM and PPM, quantized impulse modulations, PCM, differential PCM, line codes: unipolar and bipolar NRZ and RZ. Gray coding. Binary digital modulations: OOK, BPSK, FSK and CPFSK. Transmission bandwidth. Relationship between total signal-to-noise ratio, signal-to-noise ratio per bit and spectral efficiency. Multilevel modulations: M-PAM, M-PSK (QPSK and OQPSK), QAM. Transmission bandwidth and spectral efficiency. Probability of error in digital modulations: decision regions and maximum likelihood receiver. Optimal receiver schemes. Error bound.
Structure and characteristics of communication networks: generalities
Telephone network. Structure of an automatic telephone exchange
Architecture of connection networks. No-blocking condition
Data transmission networks and computer communication networks. Protocols: ISO/OSI model
Fast packet switching (FPS) and circuit switching (FCS)
Issues concerning the interconnection of telecommunication networks
Routing techniques in fixed and wireless networks
teaching_methods: In-depth seminars held by qualified external personnel
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on an oral exam. Evaluation ranges from insufficient (serious conceptual errors, fragmented understanding, inability to apply knowledge) to excellent (complete, in-depth knowledge, autonomous and flexible operation, critical skills, originality, rigor). A grade of 18-22 indicates elementary knowledge, 23-25 satisfactory understanding, 26-28 good theoretical understanding, and 29-30 cum laude excellent knowledge.
